points.requirement: An individual binding affinity is measured under stated assay conditions; for the fictional one-to-one comparison lower KD means tighter binding.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Affinity describes one binding interaction under stated conditions. For a simple one-to-one equilibrium a lower dissociation constant (KD, a concentration often given in nanomolar units) means tighter binding, whereas papers that report association constants (per molar) read the other way, with a higher value meaning tighter binding, so compare like with like.
evidence.explanation: Selected fields carry the stated distinction at their defined model, inference or source depth. Ways and Parham measured association constants in a named antibody/cell system. The KD direction is a simple one-to-one model definition, not an empirical optimum. Actual unmerged contributor text; not a registered root or main claim.

points.requirement: Linked multiple contacts create avidity, with spacing and reconnection relevant to the observed interaction.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Avidity is the combined strength of several contacts and depends on target density, spacing and the number of binding sites.
evidence.explanation: Selected fields carry the stated distinction at their defined model, inference or source depth. Ways and Parham distinguish univalent from bivalent cell binding. The indexed MICAD chapter text describes binding, rebinding and steric feasibility; it is review/background evidence, not a new primary demonstration of every schematic spacing. Actual unmerged contributor text; not a registered root or main claim.

points.requirement: Multivalent apparent cell binding is not automatically single-site affinity; target density, spacing and assay preparation matter.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Avidity is the combined strength of several contacts and depends on target density, spacing and the number of binding sites. In one set of experiments the Fab fragment of an anti-HLA-A2 antibody had an affinity of 1.9 x 10^7 per molar while the bivalent F(ab)2 or IgG showed an avidity of 1.3 x 10^9 per molar on cells (Ways and Parham, 1983). A cell-binding result for a multivalent product is therefore not its single-site affinity; ask which assay was used and how many sites took part.
evidence.explanation: Selected fields carry the stated distinction at their defined model, inference or source depth. The model distinguishes intrinsic one-site interaction from observed multivalent binding. Target density, spacing and preparation are assay-reading qualifications, not a universal numerical correction. Actual unmerged contributor text; not a registered root or main claim.

points.requirement: Native epitope accessibility is a separate question: folding or neighbouring material can block access despite target abundance or a recognized sequence.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: The epitope an antibody recognises can be a continuous stretch of sequence or a surface formed by folding, so distant parts of the chain can meet; accessibility matters, and binding to an isolated protein does not show the same site is reachable on an intact cell.
evidence.explanation: Selected fields carry the stated distinction at their defined model, inference or source depth. The current epitope definition carries folding and accessibility; the reused Bluemel abstract demonstrates geometry-dependent activity in engineered MCSP/CHO systems. Neither establishes universal tissue access from protein abundance. Registered local-root text; not main/live or independent acceptance.

points.requirement: Stability, aggregation and unwanted recognition/developability need separate tests from affinity.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Developability asks whether a molecule can be produced, purified, formulated and stored, stays soluble and stable, does not aggregate and does not bind unrelated molecules.
evidence.explanation: Selected fields carry the stated distinction at their defined model, inference or source depth. Jain measured a dozen biophysical properties on matched IgG1 preparations from 137 clinical-stage antibody sequences. Q6B separates characterization dimensions. No optimal threshold or clinical validation is inferred. Actual unmerged contributor text; not a registered root or main claim.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Stability is read from thermal unfolding and aggregation, which depend on formulation, concentration and stress. A potency assay shows activity in that assay only. FDA Q6B ties specifications to the individual product, so no universal developability cutoff exists, and tests consume candidate material and may need target protein or cells.
evidence.explanation: Selected fields carry the stated distinction at their defined model, inference or source depth. Jain measured a dozen biophysical properties on matched IgG1 preparations from 137 clinical-stage antibody sequences. Q6B separates characterization dimensions. No optimal threshold or clinical validation is inferred. Actual unmerged contributor text; not a registered root or main claim.

points.requirement: A stronger measured interaction does not establish better delivery or a safer or more effective treatment; no universal optimum is depicted.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: In mice bearing SK-OV-3 human ovarian carcinoma xenografts, four affinity variants of one anti-HER2 antibody that recognise the same epitope (monovalent KD 270 to 0.56 nmol/L) showed the highest tumour accumulation at moderate affinity; the highest-affinity antibodies stayed in the perivascular space (average penetration 20.4 um versus 84.8 um for the lowest affinity), a conditional result in that model, not an ideal affinity (Rudnick et al., 2011).
evidence.explanation: Selected fields carry the stated distinction at their defined model, inference or source depth. The Rudnick abstract and two selected complete body paragraphs give a conditional comparison in scid mice with SK-OV-3 xenografts. The biodistribution protocol used 20 micrograms intravenously; the tissue-distance analysis used 500 micrograms intraperitoneally. These are distinct readouts and protocols, not a transferable affinity optimum or patient-treatment ranking. Actual unmerged contributor text; not a registered root or main claim.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Neither study tests whether a candidate works or is safe in patients, so developable does not mean effective or safe.

A binder profile is a development framework, not a validated score, and it is retested once the binder becomes an antibody, a payload carrier or a receptor.

points.requirement: An scFv links VH and VL variable domains by a peptide linker in one protein chain; one chain is not one variable domain.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Definitions. A conventional antibody pairs heavy- and light-chain variable domains to form a binding site. A single-chain variable fragment (scFv) joins those two domains with a peptide linker in one polypeptide chain, so single-chain does not mean one variable domain (Huston et al., 1988, a 15-amino-acid linker).
evidence.explanation: Selected fields carry the stated distinction at their defined model, inference or source depth. Huston reports linked VH/VL, one chain and a tested anti-digoxin construct.
